title: Windows checkout without symlink support builds an empty mlflow-skinny/mlflow-tracing wheel
answers: mlflow-skinny wheel built from source has no modules and import mlflow fails on Windows
pip install ./libs/skinny succeeds but the package is empty
mlflow-tracing build produces wheel with zero .py files after cloning on Windows
setuptools finds no packages for libs/skinny/mlflow symlink
body:
Symptom: On Windows (no Developer Mode, core.symlinks=false) building mlflow-skinny or mlflow-tracing from a source checkout exits 0 and installs, but the wheel contains no Python modules and `import mlflow` fails.
Root cause: libs/skinny/mlflow and libs/tracing/mlflow are git symlinks (mode 120000) to the repo's mlflow package. Without symlink support git writes them as text files, so [tool.setuptools.packages.find] in the generated pyproject.toml discovers zero packages and setuptools does not error.
Fix pattern: Add a setup.py beside the generated pyproject.toml that checks Path(__file__).parent / "mlflow" is a directory and raises SystemExit with the fix (git -c core.symlinks=true clone ...). Otherwise call setup() with no arguments.
Constraints: Linux CI and PyPI builds resolve the symlink, so the guard is a no-op there. It only fails the build; it does not repoint packaging (that larger option was deferred).
applies: Build-time check for libs/skinny and libs/tracing source builds only; does not cover other packages in the monorepo.
says: Building the skinny package from source on Windows creates an empty installation without modules
Installing the tracing package from a local checkout on Windows succeeds but importing fails
Source builds on Windows silently generate wheels containing zero files when cloned without symlinks
Fail the build with helpful clone instructions when symlink support is disabled on Windows
Package installation from repository checkout installs nothing on Windows developer machines
search: Source builds for `mlflow-skinny` and `mlflow-tracing` on Windows must verify that the `mlflow` symlink is a directory rather than a plain text file. `libs/skinny/setup.py` and `libs/tracing/setup.py` check `Path(__file__).parent / 'mlflow'` and raise `SystemExit` with `git -c core.symlinks=true clone` instructions if symlinks were not enabled, otherwise calling `setup()`. Applies only to build-time checks for `libs/skinny` and `libs/tracing` source builds on Windows; it does not repoint packaging and is a no-op on Linux CI and PyPI builds.
